relevance_note: Case series of three patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variants plus relatives carrying the same variants ("He had a heterozygous c.574G>A (p.Glu192Lys) variant of TNFAIP3."), i.e. identifiable individuals with a TNFAIP3 variant.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown file, including the converted Supplementary material. No script transcribed a table: every span was copied by hand from the paper and each span was re-checked against the file. Patients-as-columns table: Table 1 (data columns P1, P2, P3). Supplementary Table S1 is also patient-as-column, but its header is garbled ("Patient No. a2-6 years P1 a≧20 years P2 P3") and several rows hold stacked value pairs (normal range / patient value), so nothing was assigned from it by position. Contradictions and unresolved points: (1) Table 1 gives "Age of onset 12 y" for P2 while the text says abdominal pain from around the age of 12 and recurrent fever around 13 years of age (the table was used for age_at_onset, the text onsets for the features); (2) Table 1 lists "hemorrhoids" for the father of P1, recorded as a feature but not mapped to any checklist item; (3) the Discussion prints Glu192Lys for the father of P1 ("patient 1 and his father with Glu192Lys") while his own sentences say only "the same variant" - his variant row keeps "Glu192Lys", but zygosity, type, pathogenicity and functional evidence were left not reported for him, as for the other relatives; (4) patient 3's "facial erythema" was not mapped to the checklist item "skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)"; (5) the abstract mentions "aphthous stomatitis" (PFAPA criteria) but no individual-level statement is printed for P1, so oral ulcers are "not reported" for him; (6) negative work-up statements that name no abnormality of their own (e.g. "no significant pathogens were detected") were not turned into features; (7) publications.cohort_size_as_stated is 3, the three patients the authors describe; the paper also states that Glu192Lys "was identified among 55 patients suspected of having autoinflammatory diseases analyzed at Gifu University Hospital", but those other patients are not described individually and their number is not stated as the study's total; (8) the asymptomatic parents (mother of P2, father of P3) get no phenotypic_features rows, because "lacked any symptoms" names no feature; (9) checklist status/evidence_basis cells carry a supporting span where the status is not 'not reported'.

functional_evidence_statement.value: NF-κB reporter gene activity not suppressed; protein expression similar to WT; A20 Ser381 phosphorylation not decreased; deubiquitinase function retained
span: The inhibitory effect on NF-κB reporter gene activity was significantly disrupted by TNFAIP3 Glu192Lys compared with that of WT upon stimulation with TNF-α or co-transfection of MYD88 and CARD11
The levels of protein expression for myc-tagged TNFAIP3 variants Glu192Lys and Gln709Arg were similar to the WT expression levels, while that of Ile310Thr was mildly decreased but not abolished.
IKKβ-mediated A20 phosphorylation levels of the variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, and Gln709Arg were similar to that of the WT
The variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, Gln709Arg, and Cys243Tyr did not show differences in deubiquitination from the WT
